statement.p: How many 11-letter words contain exactly 3 vowels? (For example, an 8-letter word with 5 vowels is aaioobtt; dont consider y a vowel for this exercise.)
What if repeated letters were not allowed?

solution.p: With repeated letters allowed, we select which 3 of the 11 letters will be vowels, then pick one of the 5 vowels for each spot, and finally pick one of the other 21 letters for each of the remaining 8 spots. Thus, {11 \choose 3}5^3 21^{8} words.

Without repeats, we still pick the positions of the vowels, but now each time we place a vowel there, we have one fewer choice for the next one. Similarly, we cannot repeat the consonants. We get {11 \choose 3}P(5,3) P(21, 8) words.
